settings.label: Notify when an update is available
Allowed emails (Webex)
settings.description: Webex account emails permitted to DM the bot. Empty = nobody (fail closed) — anyone in an org can message a Webex bot, so add only your own.

settings.label: Allowed enterprise orgs (Slack)
settings.description: Enterprise Grid org IDs to allow (starts with E or T). Leave empty to allow all orgs.

settings.label: Allowed handles (iMessage)
settings.description: Phone numbers or Apple Account emails allowed to message the agent. Empty denies everyone — anyone who knows this Mac's handle can send to it, so there is no safe default. Formatting is ignored.

settings.label: Allowed numbers (WhatsApp)
settings.description: Phone numbers (digits with country code, no plus sign) that may also chat with the agent. Empty adds nobody beyond you.

settings.label: Allowed space IDs (Webex)
settings.description:
Empty means no space is answered, so turning the switch on alone grants nothing. The sender must also be on the allowed-emails list. A space ID is an opaque string — list yours with:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $WEBEX_BOT_TOKEN" https://webexapis.com/v1/rooms

settings.label: Allowed user IDs (WeChat)
settings.description: Allowed WeChat user IDs. Empty = deny all (fail closed).

settings.label: Allowed users (email or AAD object id) (Teams)
settings.description: Azure AD UPNs/emails OR object ids permitted to DM the bot. Teams activities reliably carry the object id (email is often absent), so object ids work out of the box. Empty = nobody (fail closed).

settings.label: Answer in group spaces (Webex)
settings.description: Off by default. A reply in a space is visible to everyone in it, including people not on the allowed-emails list.

settings.label: App password (client secret) (Teams)
settings.description: Azure Bot client secret. Stored only in .env (never config.json).

settings.label: Enable iMessage channel (iMessage)
settings.description: Start the channel at gateway boot on this Mac.

settings.label: Enable Teams channel (Teams)
settings.description: Start the channel at gateway boot when the App ID + password are set.

settings.label: Enable Webex channel (Webex)
settings.description: Start the channel at gateway boot when a token is set.

settings.label: Folder name (Discord)
settings.description: Created for you when you save these settings, if it does not exist yet.

settings.description: Created for you when you save these settings, if it does not exist yet.

settings.label: Folder name (WhatsApp)
settings.description: Created for you when you turn this on, if it does not already exist.

settings.label: Hard context threshold % (Teams)
settings.description: Compact automatically at this percentage, even without a reply, so the context window never overflows.

settings.label: Hard context threshold % (Webex)
settings.description: Compact automatically at this point, even without a decision, so the context window never overflows.

settings.label: Messages database path (iMessage)
settings.description: Override where the Messages database is read from. Leave empty to use the default location.

settings.label: Owner Slack member ID (Slack)
settings.description: The one member who can always interact with the bot (KIROCREW_OWNER_ID). Starts with U or W.

settings.label: Phase reactions (Slack)
settings.description: Show phase-aware emoji reactions (queued → thinking → coding → done) on messages.

settings.label: Reply in thread (Webex)
settings.description: Reply under the message's own thread when it has one, which keeps a busy space readable.

settings.label: Send replies over (iMessage)
settings.description: Which service outbound replies use. Inbound is unaffected — messages are accepted whichever service they arrive over.

settings.label: Show thinking (Slack)
settings.description: Post the model's reasoning as a thread reply. Disable to keep responses concise.

settings.label: Slack app token (Slack)
settings.description: App-level token required for Socket Mode (starts with xapp-).

settings.label: Slack bot token (Slack)
settings.description: From OAuth & Permissions after installing your Slack app (starts with xoxb-).

settings.label: Slash command (Slack)
settings.description: Trigger word for the Slack slash command (without the leading /).

settings.label: Soft context threshold % (Webex)
settings.description: When a conversation's context passes this, suggest /compact or /new instead of compacting automatically.

settings.label: Tenant ID (Teams)
settings.description: Optional — only for single-tenant bots.

settings.label: Webex bot token (Webex)
settings.description: Bot access token from developer.webex.com (My Webex Apps).

settings.label: Auto-Compact Threshold
settings.description: Context usage % at which auto-compaction triggers. Lower = more frequent compaction, longer sessions

settings.label: Auto-Open Git in Side Panel
settings.description: Expand the side panel to the Git tab each time you start a chat in a git project. The Git tab is created either way.

settings.label: Completion Event Truncation
settings.description: Which part of a subagent's stream to keep when injecting its completion event into the parent session. Head preserves the start (default, matches legacy behavior). Tail preserves the final summary. Both keeps a slice from each end with a marker between them.

settings.label: Confirm Before Closing Session
settings.description: Show a confirmation dialog when closing a session

settings.label: Content Width
settings.description: Compact is the original view. Comfortable and Full use more screen space.

settings.label: Default Memory Mode
settings.description: Persistent uses what it knows and saves new memory. Incognito uses what it knows but saves no new memory. Temporary starts blank and saves no new memory. Every chat still appears in History. You can change the mode for any chat.

settings.label: Default Model
settings.description: Which model new sessions start with when their agent pins none. Set a model per agent under Capabilities → Agents, or pick one inside a session to override it there.

settings.label: Default Reasoning Effort
settings.description: How long models think before answering by default. Higher is slower and costs more. Only available on reasoning-capable models (Opus, Sonnet, Fable, GPT-5.x).

settings.label: Default to Autopilot Mode
settings.description: New sessions start in autopilot mode (plan → approve → execute). You can still toggle individual sessions.

settings.label: Describe your role
settings.description: Kiro uses this description to adapt vocabulary and examples to your role.

settings.label: File Change Chips
settings.description: How file diff chips appear below assistant messages

settings.label: Folder suggestions
settings.description: Offer to file a new session into a matching folder once it has a title.

settings.label: Follow-Up Bar Layout
settings.description: Multiline wraps suggestions onto multiple rows. Single line keeps them on one horizontally-scrollable row.

settings.label: History Expanded
settings.description: Expand history sidebar by default

settings.label: Link Previews
settings.description: Show a favicon and page title instead of the raw URL. This machine then fetches every link the model outputs, so each linked site sees a request from your IP address.

settings.label: MCP Apps in Side Panel
settings.description: Render interactive MCP Apps (such as Excalidraw diagrams) in the right side panel instead of inline in the chat. The panel opens automatically.

settings.label: Merge Queued Messages
settings.description: Combine follow-up messages into a single labeled prompt while the agent is busy

settings.label: Pin the latest turn
settings.description: Keep the most recent turn visible as a sticky banner once it scrolls above the fold.

settings.label: Plain diffs
settings.description: Render diffs as plain unified-diff text instead of syntax-highlighted colour. Uses less memory on large diffs.

settings.label: PR and Issue Chips on Session Cards
settings.description: Show a chip on each session's sidebar card for every pull request, merge request and issue mentioned in that session. Turning it off also stops the periodic provider calls that keep those chips up to date.

settings.label: Prevent sleep while running
settings.description: Keep your computer awake while a task is running

settings.label: Response Verbosity
settings.description: How terse the agent's prose is. Ultra-concise keeps the whole reply short: answer first, bullets over paragraphs, no filler. Code, commands, and error strings stay verbatim at every level; security warnings always appear but stay brief, and multi-step instructions stay complete. Answer-only goes further and drops explanation entirely: one sentence at most, and detail only when you ask for it — or when a decision is consequential enough (security, exposure, data loss, spend, anything hard to undo) that you need the reasoning to choose correctly.

settings.label: Restore Sessions
settings.description: Re-open recently active sessions on startup

settings.label: Restore Window
settings.description: Time window for session restoration

settings.label: Session summaries
settings.description: Summarize each session by intent. Uses tokens on turns that change the session.

settings.label: Show Context Percentage
settings.description: Display usage percentage next to the context progress bar

settings.label: Show Context Tokens
settings.description: Display used and total tokens next to the context progress bar

settings.label: Show Thinking Inline
settings.description: Show intermediate reasoning text between tool calls instead of collapsing everything

settings.label: Show Timestamps
settings.description: Display time on each message

settings.label: Simplified Tool Call Names
settings.description: When enabled, inline tool pills show simplified tool use purpose instead of the exact command being run

settings.label: Tail-only Fork
settings.description: Fork keeps only the messages after the chosen point instead of those up to it.

settings.label: Technical Comfort
settings.description: Sets how deep explanations go — plain language vs. full technical detail

settings.label: Text Streaming Style
settings.description: Immediate mode shows raw chunks as they arrive. Smooth mode buffers and fades text in at a steady pace.

settings.label: What Enter does while the agent is working
Widget Density
settings.description: How aggressively the agent uses inline widgets for visual content

settings.label: Your Role
settings.description: Kiro matches vocabulary and examples to your professional background

settings.label: Attach screenshots
settings.description: Also capture the target window and pass its file path. The accessibility tree stays the primary channel; windows containing a password field are never captured.

settings.label: Enable computer use
settings.description: Let the agent read desktop app windows through accessibility and act on their controls. Off until you turn it on here — an agent cannot enable it.

settings.label: Max tree nodes
settings.description: How many controls one window reading returns. A window with more than this gets truncated, and the agent is told so. Raise it for dense apps (a spreadsheet, an IDE); lower it to spend fewer tokens per reading.

settings.label: Screenshot width
settings.description: Longest edge of the screenshot, in pixels. Smaller is cheaper and faster to read; larger keeps small text legible if the agent has to fall back to the image.

settings.label: Show cursor motion
settings.description: Draw a cursor that glides to each target and pulses when it clicks, so you can follow along on screen. Purely visual — it changes nothing about what the agent is allowed to do, and it only appears for clicks that move the real pointer.

settings.label: Chat on a crew
settings.description: Adds “New chat on crew” to the create menu, which starts a session on a remote instance — another machine you have connected under Settings > Remote Instances. Unfinished: the session opens in that instance’s own pane and is not listed in this dashboard’s sessions yet, so to return to it later, switch to that instance’s pane.

settings.label: Crew Members
settings.description: The Crew Members page: every agent you have, each with its own thread. Still being built, so it is not offered until you turn this on.

settings.label: Developer Mode
settings.description: Show Developer page in sidebar with Logs, System metrics, and Memory internals

settings.label: Run a local gateway
settings.description: Start a gateway on this machine. Turn it off to use Kiro Crew as a client only, connecting to the gateway you have configured instead of running one here. Takes effect next time you open the app.

settings.label: Webhooks
settings.description: Inbound webhook tokens, registered contexts, and run history. The API works; the page is not finished.

settings.label: Command completion
settings.description: Show the completion popup while typing in the Terminal. Enter runs the line you typed; to take a suggestion, press ↑/↓ then Enter, or Tab. Off hides the popup; your shell's own Tab completion still works.

settings.label: Default for New Sessions
settings.description: None, auto-cycle, or pick a fixed color.

settings.label: Default shell
settings.description: Shell the built-in terminal launches — an absolute path or a command on PATH. Leave empty to use the system default ($SHELL).

settings.label: Display Mode
settings.description: How the session color is applied to the row.

settings.label: Font
settings.description: Font for the built-in terminal. Pick one installed on the machine you view the dashboard from, or type any font name — a Nerd Font renders Powerline and prompt-theme glyphs.

settings.label: Font Family
settings.description: UI font family for the dashboard. Code font follows the active theme, except OpenDyslexic which supplies its own.

settings.label: Font size
settings.description: Text size in the built-in terminal, measured in pixels.

settings.label: Highlight recent sessions
settings.description: Highlight the N most-recently-active sessions with a graded accent stripe (0 = off). Saved to your Kiro Crew config.

settings.label: Intensity
settings.description: How visible the color tint is on sidebar rows.

settings.label: Interface
settings.description: Chat bubbles or CLI-style line-by-line output

settings.label: Language
settings.description: Language for the dashboard interface.

settings.label: Mode
settings.description: Light or dark appearance for the dashboard

settings.label: Palette
settings.description: Choose a color palette for your sidebar sessions.

settings.label: Theme
settings.description: Select a theme for the dashboard

settings.label: Auto-connect crews
settings.description: When on, opening the web app connects every crew automatically, and reconnects them when you come back to the tab. Turn off to connect a crew only when you switch to it.

settings.label: Agent replies
settings.description: When the agent finishes a turn in any chat

settings.label: Approval
settings.description: Tool approval requests

settings.label: Cron
settings.description: Scheduled job completions

settings.label: Default (all categories)
settings.description: Fallback sound when no category-specific override is set

settings.label: Heartbeat
settings.description: Heartbeat task results

settings.label: Notify when a background chat finishes
settings.description: Shows a system notification naming the chat that finished, but only while this window is minimized or behind another app.

settings.label: Proactive agent messages
settings.description: When the agent proactively messages you outside a chat

settings.label: Skills
settings.description: New skill candidates awaiting your approval

settings.label: Sources
settings.description: Mute notification sources or override their priority. Muted notifications stay in history but never badge, sound, or banner.

settings.label: Subagent
settings.description: Background subagent completions

settings.label: Tasks
settings.description: Task Runner completions

settings.label: Webhook
settings.description: External hook triggers

settings.label: Send anonymous usage heartbeat
settings.description: Saved for future launches.

settings.label: Jira API token
settings.description: Authenticates Jira issue lookups for the configured instance.

settings.label: WakaTime API key
settings.description: Authenticates coding-activity sync when WakaTime is enabled.

settings.label: Trust every third-party app
settings.description: Off by default. When on, every third-party app you install can run its own code straight away, without asking you first.

settings.label: Your custom denies
settings.description: Add your own deny patterns (Python-compatible regex). These are enforced at {{productName}}'s PreToolUse gate alongside the built-in rules.

settings.label: Use ⌃ Ctrl (not ⌥ Option) for chat 1–9
settings.description: Bind chat-tab switching to Ctrl+digit instead of Option+digit

settings.label: Auto-generate skills from sessions
settings.description: Analyze each completed session and draft a reusable SKILL.md when the session demonstrates a recurring procedure — one a future session, working on a different target, would run again. Off by default. Drafts are staged to the pending queue on the Skills tab for review — nothing goes live without your approval (see below).

settings.label: Require approval before generated skills go live
settings.description: Keep every auto-generated candidate in the pending queue until you approve it. Turning this off lets prose-only skills publish automatically; skills that bundle scripts always require approval regardless.

settings.label: Auto-speak Responses
settings.description: Speak every assistant reply automatically

settings.label: Auto-submit when I finish speaking
settings.description: Use a fast model to detect when you've finished a complete request and send it automatically. Streaming providers only.

settings.label: AWS Profile (Amazon Polly)
settings.description: AWS credentials profile for Amazon Polly

settings.label: AWS Profile (Transcribe)
settings.description: AWS credentials profile for Transcribe (blank = default chain)

settings.label: AWS Region (Amazon Polly)
settings.description: AWS region for Amazon Polly API

settings.label: AWS Region (Transcribe)
settings.description: AWS region for Transcribe

settings.label: Dictation panel
settings.description: Show an animated panel while recording instead of the thin status bar. Falls back to the bar when the browser lacks WebGL2 or your system requests reduced motion.

settings.label: Enabled
settings.description: Transcribe voice into the message box when you click the mic

settings.label: Engine
settings.description: Amazon Polly engine type

settings.label: Live transcript refresh (ms)
settings.description: How often the transcript is redrawn while you speak. Lower feels more immediate and costs more processing.

settings.label: Microphone
settings.description: Input device used to capture your voice

settings.label: Model
settings.description: Models download on demand. Select one and click Download now; the desktop app already includes every other runtime dependency.

settings.label: Pause that ends a phrase (ms)
settings.description: How much silence commits what you just said. Lower reacts sooner; higher tolerates thinking pauses.

settings.label: Piper Binary
settings.description: Path to the piper executable. Leave blank to auto-detect on PATH or in a ~/piper-venv install

settings.label: Piper Model
settings.description: Path to the Piper voice model (.onnx). Required — download from huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices

settings.label: Provider
settings.description: Local speech recognition runs on this machine and sends nothing anywhere. Transcribe uploads your audio to AWS.

settings.label: Provider
settings.description: The built-in engine needs no setup; Piper is offline with better quality; Amazon Polly uses AWS credentials + network

settings.label: Speed
settings.description: Speech rate for spoken replies (built-in engine)

settings.label: Speed
settings.description: Speech rate for spoken replies (Amazon Polly)

settings.label: Speed
settings.description: Piper speech speed (length scale)

settings.label: Streaming
settings.description: Show the transcript in the input box as you speak, instead of only when you stop.

settings.label: Tap vs. hold cutoff
settings.description: Only used by “Both”. Hold the key longer than this to talk; a quicker tap starts recording and leaves it on.

settings.label: Voice
settings.description: Voice from the host's built-in speech engine

settings.label: Voice
settings.description: Amazon Polly voice for TTS
